passage: Before I signed anything in Pune, I took a Friday off and went there for the weekend. My listings had promised "ten minutes to the office" in three different places. So at half past five, the worst hour, I rode the route from the office to each address, and each time the ten minutes turned into forty. On Saturday I walked three areas end to end: the lane behind the market, the quiet colony with the tree-lined road, the new towers near the highway. I bought tea at a stall in each and asked the vendor what the place was like at night. One was loud, one had no shops, one felt right. My wife Ishita, on the phone, asked, "And the photos?" I said, "The photos didn't show the traffic." I signed for the third area on Sunday. - Kiran

Relocation coordinator's note — Irfan, transfer from Jaipur to the Hyderabad office. Written by Noor.

Most transferees ask me for a list of "good areas" and sign the first lease a broker shows them. Irfan asked for three days' leave instead.
He arrived on a Thursday and did something simple: he travelled to our office from three different areas at peak hour. Gachibowli, Kondapur and Miyapur. He timed each trip on both mornings, eight-thirty and nine. He walked around each area in the evening, looked at the markets, checked where the nearest clinic was.
On Saturday he messaged me: "Kondapur looks fine online, but the morning traffic is forty-five minutes. Miyapur has the metro; it's thirty-five, reliable."
He signed a lease in Miyapur the following week.
What I did next: I've added a line to our relocation guide suggesting a peak-hour visit before signing.

How might Irfan have felt after timing the commutes himself?
qa.a: He likely felt more confident and reassured, trusting his own experience rather than online guesses.

qa.q: What else could Irfan check before signing the lease?
qa.a: He could ask colleagues who moved earlier about broker fees and landlord issues in Miyapur.

qa.q: How does Irfan's approach look to the relocation coordinator?
qa.a: The coordinator sees it as a model, adding a peak-hour visit to the relocation guide for others.

grounding: It shows someone spending time in the new city, checking peak-hour commutes and visiting three areas before signing a lease, replacing online guesses with experience.

passage:
Saturday night, Chennai

Came here for the weekend before the transfer starts next month. Dhruv let me stay on his sofa.
Online, Velachery looked perfect: cheaper rent, big malls, good reviews. So this morning at eight-forty-five I took the bus from Velachery to the office in Guindy. Fifty minutes, standing, in the heat. Tried it again at nine-thirty. Forty.
Then Dhruv drove me to Adyar and Nungambakkam. Walked around both in the afternoon. Adyar felt quiet, green, a proper vegetable market, and the train to Guindy took twenty minutes.
Online, I'd have signed for Velachery by now. In person, I'd hate that commute within a week.
Tomorrow I'm seeing two flats in Adyar. Rent is a little higher, but I'll get back an hour a day.
Glad I came instead of guessing.
— Thomas

qa.a: Dhruv gives Thomas a place to stay and drives Thomas around, which makes the visits possible and turns guesswork into first-hand experience.
